criteria.text: The participant has a histologically or cytologically confirmed diagnosis of any type of solid tumor malignancy or lymphoma.

In the Phase 1 Dose Escalation portion, the participant has any advanced solid tumor of Head and Neck Cancers (of any types), Esophageal cancer, Lung cancers (of any types), Mesothelioma, or Pancreatic cancers.

In the Phase 1 Dose Escalation portion, the participant has any NTRK1 gene fusion positive ("NTRK1+") solid tumors or lymphomas, that is relapsed, refractory or intolerant (R/R/I) to standard of care (SOC) and for which there is no approved or curative therapy. Additionally, patients must not be candidates for or have exhausted regimens known to provide clinical benefit, including hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in lymphoma patients if they are deemed transplant eligible.

In the Phase 2 Monotherapy and Combination with Pembrolizumab portion, the participant must have TrkA-driven HNC, Esophageal, Lung, Mesothelioma, Pancreatic cancers; or, any NTRK1+ solid tumors or lymphoma*, that is R/R/I to SOC.
The participant has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 0 or 1.
The participant is able to swallow and retain oral medication.
The participant either has available archival tumor tissue samples, or consents to tumor tissue sampling prior to the first dose.

The participant has adequate organ system function as defined as follows: Absolute neutrophil count ≥1.5x10^9/L, Hemoglobin ≥9g/dL, Platelets ≥100x10^9/L, PT/INR, PTT ≤1.5xULN, Total bilirubin ≤1.5x ULN, AST, ALT ≤2.5xULN, Creatinine ≤1.2xULN for age, weight, Calculated creatinine clearance or 24h urine creatinine clearance ≥60mL/min.
The participant received chemotherapy having delayed toxicity within the last 14 days (six weeks for prior nitrosourea or mitomycin C).
The participant received anticancer therapy with radiation, immunotherapy, and a biologic, surgery and/or tumor embolization within the past 2 weeks.

The participant received an investigational anticancer drug within 14 days or 5 half-lives of the investigational agent, whichever is longer, prior to the first dose of VMD-928. Any exceptions to the above must be approved by the Sponsor Medical Monitor.
The participant has unresolved toxicity from previous anticancer therapy > CTCAE Grade 1 (except alopecia or anemia) unless agreed to by both the Sponsor Medical Monitor and the Investigator.
The participant has a known active infection including HIV disease.
The participant is currently pregnant, nursing, or planning to become pregnant during the course of the study.
The participant has a QTcF interval ≥ 480 msec.
The participant has Class II, III, or IV heart failure as defined by the New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional classification system.
The participant has acute coronary syndromes (including unstable angina), coronary angioplasty, or stenting within the past 24 weeks.
The participant has unstable or uncompensated respiratory, hepatic, renal, or cardiac disease that would compromise the patient's safety or interfere with assessment of the drug.

The participant has psychological, familial, sociological, geographical, or other concurrent conditions that would interfere with safety evaluation, limit the patient's ability to follow the procedures in the protocol or otherwise jeopardize compliance with the protocol. Patients with uncontrolled major depression, bipolar disorder, or severe anxiety disorder are excluded.
The participant has had or is currently having other malignant tumors within 3 years.
The participant has multiple factors that affect their oral medication.
The participant has long-term unhealed wounds or fractures.
The participant has uncontrolled pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, or ascites that still require repeated drainage.

The participant is taking the following drugs and can't stop them during the study: Tylenol or medicine containing acetaminophen (paracetamol). Antacids (e.g. TUMS, calcium carbonate, or magnesium hydroxide), proton pump inhibitors (e.g. omeprazole), H2 blockers (e.g. famotidine), or buffered vitamins.
The participant has Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) negative nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
In the Phase 2 portion, the participant has a negative result on TrkA immunohistochemistry (IHC) assay.
The participant has a visceral crisis, defined as severe organ dysfunction and rapid progression of the cancer. (It is not about presence of visceral metastasis.)

In the combination therapy with Pembrolizumab portion, the participant has serious adverse immune related adverse events (grade 3 or 4) with previous PD-1(L1) inhibitor therapy, that were symptomatic and required prolong immunosuppression (>6 weeks).
The participant has any grade Pneumonitis and Myocarditis related to prior PD-1(L1) inhibitor therapy.
For subjects that received PD-1(L1) inhibitors before, there should be a washout period of at least 21 days between the last day of PD-1(L1) inhibitor and first day of study medications.
The participant relapsed after prior treatment with PD-1(L1) inhibitors. Relapsed is defined as patients having best overall response of CR or PR after treatment with a PD-1(L1) inhibitor.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "VMD-928 Monotherapy and in Combination With Pembrolizumab to Treat TrkA Overexpression Driven Solid Tumors or Lymphoma". Your earlier answers already covered 16 of its rules. I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been diagnosed with a solid tumor or lymphoma based on a biopsy or cell sample?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, the biopsy showed squamous cell carcinoma.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been told that your cancer is NTRK1 gene fusion positive (also called NTRK1+ or TrkA overexpression)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know. That I couldn't tell you.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you able to swallow and keep down oral medications?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I can swallow pills fine. I've been taking Libtayo and carboplatin, so I know how to handle oral meds.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently experiencing any side effects from your previous cancer treatments that are moderate to severe (Grade 2 or higher), such as significant pain, nausea, or fatigue? This excludes hair loss or low blood counts.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about specific side effect grades. I just know the cancer grew on the treatment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have a known active infection, such as HIV?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Never been tested for it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently pregnant, nursing, or planning to become pregnant during the study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, on two counts.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been told by a doctor that you have a heart rhythm condition called Long QT syndrome, or that your QTcF interval is 480 msec or higher?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't been told that. I don't know about my QTcF interval.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with heart failure, or told by a doctor that you have Class II, III, or IV heart failure according to the New York Heart Association (NYHA) classification?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't been diagnosed with heart failure.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any of the following in the last 6 months: a heart attack, unstable chest pain (angina), a procedure to open a blocked heart artery (angioplasty), or placement of a stent?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any of those heart issues in the last six months.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have any unstable or uncompensated conditions affecting your lungs, liver, kidneys, or heart that might affect your safety or the study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have any unstable conditions like that. My kidney transplant was back in 2011, so it's stable.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help us ensure your safety and ability to follow the study steps, do you currently have any psychological conditions, such as uncontrolled major depression, bipolar disorder, or severe anxiety, that might make it difficult to participate?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have any of those conditions. I'm just a retired surveyor trying to get my life back on track.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently taking Tylenol (acetaminophen), antacids (like TUMS), acid reducers (like omeprazole or famotidine), or buffered vitamins?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I take no daily steroid pills, so I'm not on those. I don't know about the other specific meds like Tylenol or antacids.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.

flags.reason: The message claims the person takes oral medications ('handle oral meds'), but the facts state they have not had targeted pills ('prior_targeted: No') and do not take daily steroids ('steroids: No'), while Libtayo and carboplatin are intravenous treatments, not oral pills.

The message claims the person does not have 'any of those conditions,' which contradicts the facts stating they have squamous cell carcinoma, liver metastases, and a history of melanoma and kidney transplant.
